answer: We formalize a dynamic opportunity-cost bond whose slashing matrix is subgame-perfect, so each identity split incurs collateral exceeding any discounted gain. Under adversarial multi-agent play the resulting payoff is strictly negative, forcing a unique strict Nash equilibrium at single-identity participation. We thread the violet equilibrium through the replication game: the bond schedule acts as an exact mirror of marginal extraction, eliminating profitable Sybil deviation.
